title: A slow-growing nodule in the maxilla
html: A 51-year-old woman with a slow-growing mass of approximately 8 months of evolution came to Hospital dos Servidores do Estado de Pernambuco, Recife, Brazil. Her medical, surgical, familial, and social histories were noncontributory. No drug or food allergies and no use of medications were reported. A review of systems produced unremarkable results. The extraoral examination revealed no evidence of cervical lymphadenopathy or major salivary gland alterations. Intraorally, a firm, painless nodule in the anterior region of the right maxilla was observed, with focal erythema and telangiectasia of the overlying mucosa (Figure 1A).
